headline: Recommended a shopping cart ordinance requiring ID tags on carts and locking devices to keep them on store property.
summary: Councilor Dylan Benson said he added an exemption for businesses with fewer than 50 carts. Councilor Marjorie Grace worried that retrofitting costs would be passed on to shoppers, and Councilor Frank Margiotta raised concerns about enforcement. Fines apply only after a first written warning, and stores will get notice before the public hearing.
decisions: Recommended that the City Council add a new Article IV, Shopping Cart Regulations, to Chapter 14 of the city code, by a 2-1 roll call vote.

decision_titles: Shopping cart regulations ordinance (Chapter 14, Article IV)
plain_text:
O&A Committee November 2, 2026 Page 1 of 3
Ordinances & Administration Committee
Monday, November 2, 2026 – 6:00 p.m.
Harbormaster Conference Room
19 Harbor Loop
Gloucester, MA 01930
-Minutes-
Present: Chair, Councilor Sean Nolan; Vice Chair; Councilor Frank Margiotta (remote); Councilor 
Marjorie Grace
Other Councilors Present: Councilor Dylan Benson
This meeting was conducted in-person and remotely via ZOOM.
The meeting was called to order at 6:00 p.m.
1. CC#2026-017 (Benson): Amend GCO Ch. 14 “Offenses and Miscellaneous Provisions” by
ADDING a new Article IV “Shopping Cart Regulations,” Sec. 14-46 “Definitions,” Sec. 14-47
“Identification of shopping carts,” Sec. 14-48 “Shopping carts to be confined to premises,” Sec. 14-
49 “Enforcement.” (cont. from September 14, 2026)
Summary of Discussion: Councilor Benson stated that he had updated the proposed ordinance since the
last meeting at the request of the Committee. He stated that he had put in an exemption for businesses that
have less than 50 shopping carts. He stated that he had added some additional language under the
identification and restriction of shopping carts that the City General Counsel had suggested. He stated that
the focus on the ordinance amendment was to have businesses install restrictive devices on shopping carts.
He stated that he had reached out to Shaw’s, Stop & Shop, and Dollar General and he had sent those
communications to the Committee. He stated that he had pictures of shopping carts that he had shared with
the Committee, and would share at City Council. 
Councilor Grace stated that shopping carts being abandoned around the City was a problem but she did
have concerns that the cost of retrofitting shopping carts would be passed on to consumers. Councilor Benson
stated that communities that had implemented similar ordinances had comparable grocery prices to the City.
He stated that smaller businesses would be exempt. 
Councilor Grace asked if there was currently a program in place for businesses to retrieve abandoned carts.
Councilor Benson stated he was not aware of one, but Market Basket would retrieve their own abandoned
carts. He stated Marshall’s already had restrictive devices installed on their carts. 
Councilor Grace stated that she hoped that representatives of the grocery stores would speak at the public
hearing. Councilor Benson stated that the only fines that would be administered would be if locking systems
were not installed. He stated that some communities with similar ordinances retrieved carts and then had
businesses pay for them. 
Councilor Margiotta stated he was concerned regarding enforcement.
Councilor Nolan stated that affected stores should be given due notice before the public hearing on the
matter. Councilor Benson stated he would reach out to them.
O&A Committee November 2, 2026 Page 2 of 3
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION:  On a motion by Councilor Grace, seconded by Councilor Margiotta,
the Ordinances & Administration Committee voted by ROLL CALL 2 in favor, 1 opposed (Margiotta), to
recommend that the City Council amend the Gloucester Code of Ordinances, Chapter 14 “Offenses and
Miscellaneous Provisions” by ADDING a new Article IV as follows:
Chapter 14 – OFFENSES AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ARTICLE IV –
SHOPPING CART REGULATIONS
Sec. 14-46. Deﬁnitions.
The following terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this 
section:
Business premises means the entire area owned, leased, or utilized by the owner of a business 
establishment, including any parking lot provided for customer use.
Owner means any person who owns, leases, or otherwise has lawful possession or control of a shopping
cart supplied for customer use at a business establishment in the city, including the operator of the 
business establishment where the cart is made available to customers.
Restrictive device means a device that uses an electronic or mechanical wheel-locking mechanism designed
to prevent the unauthorized removal of a shopping cart from the business premises.
Shopping cart means any rolling basket or container commonly used in supermarkets, grocery stores, 
department stores, retail business establishments, and other stores frequented by customers.
Sec. 14-47. Identiﬁcation and Restriction of Shopping Carts.
(a) Beginning six months after the eﬀective date of this ordinance, an owner of shopping carts supplied to
customers for use within a business premises shall securely and durably aﬃx to each cart an identiﬁcation
tag displaying the name, local address, and telephone number of the owner.
(b)Beginning six months after the eﬀective date of this ordinance, an owner of shopping carts supplied to
customers for outdoor use in any parking lot shall install and maintain a system capable of preventing
the unauthorized removal of shopping carts from the business premises through the use of a restrictive
device continuously equipped to each cart.
(c) Exemption. Any owner that provides fewer than 50 shopping carts for customer use shall be exempt
from the requirements of this section.
Sec. 14-48. Enforcement.
(a) A violation of Section 14-47(a) shall be subject to the following:
(1) First oﬀense: written warning.
(2) Second and subsequent oﬀenses: a ﬁne of $10.
(3) For second or subsequent oﬀenses, each cart to which a proper identiﬁcation tag has not been aﬃxed
shall be deemed a separate oﬀense, and each day the violation continues shall constitute a separate o

ﬀense with respect to each cart.
(b) A violation of Section 14-47(b) shall be subject to the following:
(1) First oﬀense: written warning.
(2) Second and subsequent oﬀenses: a ﬁne of $300.
(3) For second or subsequent oﬀenses, each cart found without a restrictive device shall be deemed a
separate oﬀense, and each day the violation continues shall constitute a separate oﬀense with respect
to each cart.
(c) This article shall be enforced by the Building Commissioner or their designee, or by any oﬃcer of
the Police Department.
(d) This article may be enforced through any lawful means, including but not limited to noncriminal
disposition pursuant to and subject to the safeguards of M.G.L. c. 40, § 21D.
Sec. 14-49. Severability.
If any provision of this article is held to be invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity shall
not aﬀect the remaining provisions, which shall remain in full force and eﬀect.
A public hearing for this matter will be held November 24, 2026
